foskeia:abstract:1.title: Foskeia pelendonum , a new rhabdodontomorph from the Lower Cretaceous of Salas de los Infantes (Burgos Province, Spain), and a new phylogeny of ornithischian dinosaurs (abstract)

facts.statement: The genus Foskeia contains only one known species, F. pelendonum, represented by fossils of multiple individuals at different growth stages.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Foskeia pelendonum, known from fossils of multiple individuals of different ontogenetic stages.

facts.statement: Dieudonné and colleagues reported finding at least five individuals of a small, gracile ornithopod about 0.5 meters long in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, Dieudonné et al. reported the discovery of at least five individuals of a gracile, small-bodied ornithopod (approximately 0.5 m long), representing several distinct ontogenetic stages.

facts.statement: New cranial elements found later and analyzed with μCT scanning led to the formal description of the genus and species in 2026.
facts.quote: The discovery of new cranial elements in subsequent fieldwork and assessment of this material via μCT scanning allowed the remains to be formally described as a new genus and species of rhabdodontomorph ornithopod in 2026.

facts.statement: The name Foskeia comes from Ancient Greek words meaning 'light' and 'to forage', referencing the animal's small size and likely herbivory.
facts.quote: The generic name, Foskeia, is derived from the Ancient Greek words φῶς (light) and βόσκειν (to forage), referring to its small size and presumed herbivorous habits.

facts.statement: The species name pelendonum honors the Pelendones, a Celtiberian tribe from near the fossil site.
facts.quote: The specific name, pelendonum, is a reference to the Pelendones, a Celtiberian tribe from the Fuentes de Duero, near the type locality.

facts.statement: Foskeia lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Age: Early Cretaceous (Barremian–Aptian)

facts.statement: The type locality for Foskeia is the Castrillo de la Reina Formation.
facts.quote: Type locality: Castrillo de la Reina Formation

facts.statement: Foskeia fossils have been found in Spain.
facts.quote: Country: Spain

facts.statement: Juvenile Foskeia started life as quadrupeds but transitioned to bipedalism at an early stage of growth.
facts.quote: Analysis of the limb bones performed by Dieudonné et al. (2023) revealed that Foskeia juveniles began life as quadrupedal animals. However, at an early stage in their ontogeny, they transitioned to bipedalism.

facts.statement: The largest known individual was a late subadult, suggesting Foskeia was one of the smallest ornithopods.
facts.quote: Histological analysis of the limb bones further revealed that the largest known individual of Foskeia represents a late subadult, which supports the interpretation that the species was among the smallest ornithopods.

facts.statement: The shift from quadrupedal to bipedal locomotion in Foskeia is consistent with patterns seen in other early rhabdodontomorphs.
facts.quote: This postural transition is consistent with other early rhabdodontomorphs.

facts.statement: In 2026, Dieudonné and colleagues placed Foskeia in a new subclade called Rhabdodontia within Rhabdodontomorpha.
facts.quote: In 2026, upon the formal naming of the Vegagete ornithopod, Dieudonné et al. placed the taxon within a novel subclade within the Rhabdodontomorpha, which they named Rhabdodontia.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Foskeia as the sister taxon to traditional Rhabdodontidae, diverging after Muttaburrasaurus and Fostoria.
facts.quote: Foskeia was recovered diverging after Muttaburrasaurus and Fostoria, as the sister taxon to a traditional Rhabdodontidae.

facts.statement: Recent analyses place the rhabdodontomorph clade in a more advanced position at the base of Ankylopollexia.
facts.quote: Contrary to previous analyses, the rhabdodontomorph clade was placed in a more derived (advanced) position, at the base of the Ankylopollexia.

facts.statement: The species F. pelendonum was described by Dieudonné and colleagues in 2026.
facts.quote: species_authority: Dieudonné et al., 2026

facts.statement: Foskeia belongs to the class Sauropsida.
facts.quote: classis: Sauropsida

facts.statement: Foskeia is classified within the superorder Dinosauria.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria

facts.statement: Foskeia is an ornithischian dinosaur.
facts.quote: ordo: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Foskeia is classified within the infraorder Ornithopoda.
facts.quote: infraordo: Ornithopoda

facts.statement: Foskeia lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers define the new clade Rhabdodontia as a restricted group of European rhabdodontomorphs including Foskeia and rhabdodontids.
The current phylogenetic placement of rhabdodontomorphs is considered provisional pending the addition of more saurischian data.

rejected.statement: Foskeia is an extinct genus of rhabdodontomorph ornithopod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of Spain.
rejected.quote: Foskeia is an extinct genus of rhabdodontomorph ornithopod dinosaurs known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian to Aptian ages) Castrillo de la Reina Formation of Spain.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Foskeia is an extinct genus of rhabdodontomorph ornithopod'

rejected.statement: Foskeia is diagnosed by unique features including fused premaxillae, procumbent premaxillary teeth, a single filiform first dentary tooth, and an elevated craniomandibular joint.
rejected.quote: It is diagnosed by a high number of unique features such as the possession of fused premaxillae, procumbent premaxillary teeth, one filiform first dentary tooth, and an elevated craniomandibular joint.
